{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Kpone IPP (KIPP) power station''' is an operating power station of at least 350-megawatts (MW) in Tema, Greater Accra, Ghana.

==Background==

'''In October 2014''', the financial close of US $900 million of project finance to develop the Kpone Independent Power Plant (KIPP) was reached.<ref name="ref_11">{{Cite news|url=https://www.dbsa.org/case-studies/financing-cenpower-kpone-340-mw-ipp-ghana|title=Financing Cenpower Kpone 340 MW IPP, Ghana|work=Development Bank of Southern Africa|access-date=2022-07-25|language=en}}</ref> The project finance comprises a US$650 million debt tranche and a US$250 million equity tranche.<ref name="ref_11">{{Cite news|url=https://www.dbsa.org/case-studies/financing-cenpower-kpone-340-mw-ipp-ghana|title=Financing Cenpower Kpone 340 MW IPP, Ghana|work=Development Bank of Southern Africa|access-date=2022-07-25|language=en}}</ref> The power generated by this station will be sold directly to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG), for integration into the Ghanaian national electricity grid.<ref name="ref_12">{{Cite news|url=http://www.esi-africa.com/news/ghana-kpone-ipp-thermal-power-plant-making-progress/|title=Ghana: Kpone IPP thermal power plant making progress - ESI-Africa.com|date=2015-07-30|work=ESI-Africa.com|access-date=2022-07-25|language=en-US}}</ref>'''In 2015''', the project construction started.<ref name="ref_13">{{Cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kpone_Thermal_Power_Station_II|title=Kpone Thermal Power Station II|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> '''In December 2014''', the KIPP project reached its financial close.<ref name="ref_14">{{Cite web|url=https://cenpowergen.com/kipp|title=KIPP|last=Super User|website=cenpowergen.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2022-07-25}}</ref>The project was funded by six commercial banks and six Development Finance Institutions with a 15-year debt tenor.'''In June 2019''', the Kpone Independent Power Plant achieved commercial operations. It is among the largest IPPs in Ghana, accounting for approximately 10% of Ghana’s total installed capacity and approximately 15% of its available thermal generation capacity.<ref name="ref_3">{{cite web |url=https://www.cenpowergen.com/ |title=Cenpower Generation Company Limited (Cenpower or CGC) |date= |website=www.cenpowergen.com |access-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305011638/https://cenpowergen.com/ |archive-date=March 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> As a Combined Cycle Gas Turbine (CCGT) plant, it is among Ghana’s most fuel-efficient thermal power stations.<ref name="ref_3">{{cite web |url=https://www.cenpowergen.com/ |title=Cenpower Generation Company Limited (Cenpower or CGC) |date= |website=www.cenpowergen.com |access-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305011638/https://cenpowergen.com/ |archive-date=March 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> '''The plant is''': <ref name="ref_3">{{cite web |url=https://www.cenpowergen.com/ |title=Cenpower Generation Company Limited (Cenpower or CGC) |date= |website=www.cenpowergen.com |access-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305011638/https://cenpowergen.com/ |archive-date=March 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref> * The first licensed IPP in Ghana.* The first greenfield project financed IPP in Ghana, taking fuel supply risk.* The first project to provide a working capital facility through a fuel financing facility for the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG).* The first thermal IPP project financed in Sub-Saharan Africa.* Sumitomo Corporation (Japan)’s first thermal IPP investment in Africa.'''The project also received four international awards:'''<ref name="ref_11">{{Cite news|url=https://www.dbsa.org/case-studies/financing-cenpower-kpone-340-mw-ipp-ghana|title=Financing Cenpower Kpone 340 MW IPP, Ghana|work=Development Bank of Southern Africa|access-date=2022-07-25|language=en}}</ref>* The African Banker Award: African Banker’s 2015 Infrastructure Deal of the Year* The EMEA Finance Magazine: Best Power Deal in EMEA* The pan-African Africa Investor (AI) Award: AI Best Power Deal of the Year 2015* Thttps://www.vra.com/our_mandate/kpone_thermal_power_station.phphomson Reuters PFI Award (London): Africa’s Power Deal of the Year
